title: OES-32 HLS Prototype: Profile A sidecar (C++ HLS + g++ testbench)
description:
Profile A sidecar to oes32-residual: a C++14 High-Level Synthesis (HLS) research prototype of OES-32 telemetry-triage checks (coherence floor, EVEN/ODD symmetry, FOLD8 ring balance) on a 32-element vector, behind an AXI4-Lite interface declaration, with a portable g++ testbench (6 test cases, 8 checks) that runs in CI without AMD/Xilinx tools. A Vitis HLS script targets the AMD Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC ZCU111 board as a TARGET.

New in 0.2.0: streaming triage kernel. oes32_triage_accelerator is an AXI4-Stream core (ap_ctrl_none, AXI4-Lite control bundle CONTROL_BUS). It routes each telemetry packet to a primary or residual stream using an adaptive fixed-point gain τ that is clamped to [τmin, τmax] and can be reset over AXI4-Lite. A g++ testbench (19 checks, 1402 packets) compares it against a double-precision golden model on deterministic SYNTHETIC stimuli. Routing matches exactly, and τ stays within 16 LSB (2-10) of the golden value and inside its bounds. The g++ build uses the Apache-2.0 Xilinx ap_int/ap_fixed headers fetched at a pinned commit, plus a testbench-only hls_stream.h shim. The kernel is per-call (non-blocking read) and relies on continuous re-invocation; a while(1)/PIPELINE II=1 alternative is documented but not implemented.

New in 0.3.0: Python bindings and bit-exact tests. The oes32_triage extension (pybind11, scikit-build-core) compiles the unchanged C++ kernel and exposes it as TriageKernel, with per-call, raw-bit and vectorised APIs. The kernel's function-static state is handled explicitly: a fresh object starts through reset_tau, and state is restored bit-exactly through an empty-stream reset_tau call when objects interleave. A bit-accurate pure-Python reference model (oes32_triage_ref) is checked against the C++ kernel by a pytest and Hypothesis suite (36 tests, 13 property-based tests). The suite covers routing and raw τ bits on seeded and random SYNTHETIC stimuli, a zero-mismatch replay of the recorded g++ testbench trace, behavioural invariants, and the golden-model tolerance. It runs in CI on Python 3.10–3.13. An executable explainer notebook is included; its "membrane" framing is a metaphor only. This is C-simulation of the HLS source, not RTL.

Relationship to ADR-001. The normative residual R lives in oes32-residual@b77b612. The checks here differ in two documented ways: a squared difference compared to τ = 0.09 (equivalent to an absolute threshold of 0.3), and a ≥ fail rule (the normative contract fails only when R > tolerance).

Evidence tags. C++ testbenches (both kernels) and the Python test suite: SYNTHETIC inputs, run in CI. Vitis HLS synthesis, C/RTL co-simulation, II and timing for both kernels: UNRUN (the CI synthesis job is a placeholder that only echoes the commands). Latency < 20 ns, 100 MHz clock, II = 1: TARGET (design intent, no synthesis or timing report exists). Board deployment on ZCU111: UNRUN. Kuramoto example output: SYNTHETIC.

Scope and limits. Research prototype. Not synthesized, placed, routed, or run on an FPGA; not a QPU, quantum device, or quantum-hardware result; not production, certified, medical, or field hardware; not the normative OES-32 residual.

Evidence tags follow sparkainlp-x/.github (SYNTHETIC / REPORTED / TARGET / UNRUN).
